findings.ref: review #1; AC-M0-04 x M0 merge-commit regression; DoD-4 spirit
findings.where: scripts/ci/gitleaks.sh:83 (-m in the name-check git log)
findings.problem: Risky security logic without a test: removing -m from the name check leaves tests/secrets fully green (19 passed, 150 subtests), yet without it a PR whose merge commit alone adds an empty .env goes green (range exit 0; with -m exit 1). gitleaks cannot see empty files, so this line is the only defence.
findings.required_improvement: Add a test: merge commit that adds only an empty .env -> range red with 'gitleaks.sh: secret file name: .env'. Confirm it fails with -m removed.

findings.problem: `|| true` also swallows grep exit 2. With a grep without -P (BSD/busybox; simulated), `gitleaks.sh tree` on a repo with an empty .env prints 'grep: invalid option -- P' and exits 0. CI (GNU grep) not affected.
findings.required_improvement: `{ grep -zP "$NAMES" || [ $? -eq 1 ]; }` so a grep error returns 2.

findings.problem: @pytest.mark.enable_socket or the socket_enabled fixture re-enables the network per test: a test with UDP sendto to 192.0.2.1 passes (2 passed). The old guard had no opt-out; DoD-5 forbids comparable opt-outs.
findings.required_improvement: Record a DoD-style violation in conftest.py for items with the enable_socket marker or socket_enabled fixture, or note in the plan that the opt-out is accepted.
